message.content:
**Traffic Laws in Texas – A Quick Reference Guide** | Topic | Key Points | Where to Find More Info | |-------|------------|------------------------| | **Speed Limits** | • General limit: 55 mph on rural roads, 45 mph on urban roads.
• 70 mph on interstate highways (except where posted otherwise).
• 65 mph on freeways in urban areas. | Texas Department of Transportation (TxDOT) – Speed Limit Regulations | | **Seat‑belt & Child Safety** | • All drivers and passengers must wear seat belts.
• Children under 8 must be in a child safety seat or booster.
• Children under 5 must be in a rear‑facing seat. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Cell‑Phone Use** | • Hand‑held phone use while driving is prohibited.
• Hands‑free devices are allowed. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Driving Under Influence (DUI)** | • Blood Alcohol Concentration (BAC) of 0.08% or higher is illegal.
• Zero‑tolerance for drivers under 21.
• Penalties include fines, license suspension, and possible jail time. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Right‑of‑Way** | • Yield to pedestrians at crosswalks.
• Stop at red lights and stop signs.
• “Move over” law: vehicles must move over a lane if a disabled vehicle is stopped on the shoulder. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **School Bus** | • Stop for a school bus with its stop sign extended and red lights flashing.
• No passing until the bus resumes motion. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Headlights & Lighting** | • Headlights must be on from sunset to sunrise, and during rain, fog, or snow.
• Fog lights may be used when visibility is less than 200 ft. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Towing & Tow‑away** | • Towing a vehicle requires a valid license and registration.
• Tow‑away laws apply to abandoned or illegally parked vehicles. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Vehicle Registration & Insurance** | • Vehicles must be registered and display a valid license plate.
• Proof of insurance is required; minimum liability coverage is $30,000 for bodily injury per person, $60,000 per accident, and $25,000 for property damage. | Texas Department of Motor Vehicles (TxDMV) | | **Parking** | • No parking in front of fire hydrants, on sidewalks, or in designated no‑parking zones.
• Pay‑and‑display or meter parking is common in cities. | Local city ordinances | | **Lane‑Changing & Overtaking** | • Use turn signals.
• Do not cut off other drivers. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | | **Winter & Weather Conditions** | • Vehicles must be equipped with winter tires or chains in certain counties.
• Drivers must maintain safe following distances. | TxDOT Weather Advisory | | **Special Vehicle Rules** | • Motorcycles, bicycles, and scooters have specific lane and helmet requirements. | Texas Transportation Code §545.001 | ### How to Stay Updated - **TxDOT Website** – Official rules, updates, and safety campaigns. - **TxDMV** – Registration, insurance, and driver licensing information. - **Texas Transportation Code** – Full legal text (available online). - **Local County & City Ordinances** – For specific local rules (e.g., parking, speed limits). --- #### Quick Tips 1. **Always check posted signs** – Speed limits and special rules can vary by county or city. 2. **Keep your insurance documents handy** – You may need to show proof of insurance at a police checkpoint. 3. **Use hands‑free devices** – Avoid penalties for cell‑phone use while driving. 4. **Be mindful of weather** – Adjust speed and following distance during rain, fog, or snow. Feel free to ask if you need details on a specific law or how to comply with a particular regulation!
